title: Make a Website
subtitle: Plan in ChatGPT. Build. Live on Vercel.
description: Teachy runs the interview you skip, writes a great ChatGPT prompt, helps you mock and build, then ships a live Vercel URL you can text someone.
learningOutcomes: Answer sharp intake questions so an AI gets real context — not a vague one-liner
Use a Teachy-written prompt in ChatGPT to produce a concrete site plan
Generate a landing mock (and more pages only if image quota allows)
Build the site in Replit or a coding agent matched to what they already pay for
Deploy to Vercel and share a live URL

artifact.initialState: no plan, no site, nothing live
artifact.finalState: a live personal site on Vercel with a public URL
artifact.previewIfNoProgress: No website yet — let's plan one

goals.title: Figure out your path
goals.goal: Say what the site is for, what you already have, and whether you want Replit (vibe) or a coding agent.
goals.outcome: You and Teachy agree on goal, starting point, and build tool.
goals.coachAsk: Help me start Make a Website. Ask me the intake questions one at a time — goal, who gets the link, what I already have, Replit vs coding agent — and if I pick agent, ask whether I pay for ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor.
goals.doneWhen: The learner has stated (1) site goal, (2) who they will text the link to, (3) what they already have, and (4) Replit vs coding agent — and if agent, which paid AI they use or that they are unpaid / willing to pay.
tips: One question at a time — never dump the whole intake
Remember their answers for later goals (build tool + paid AI)
If they already have Figma/Canva, note that — we may skip image gens
If they only have a domain, still ship *.vercel.app first

concepts: intake before tools — route the path before opening tabs
Replit = vibe build in the browser; agent = Cursor / Claude Code / Codex
agent routing: Cursor→Cursor, Claude→Claude Code, ChatGPT→Codex/ChatGPT, unpaid→Codex free, willing to pay→Claude Code
commonMistakes: opening ChatGPT before knowing the goal
pushing a paid tool when they picked Replit
successExamples: I want a portfolio for job apps, I have nothing, I want Replit
Hustle page, I have ChatGPT HTML in Downloads, I pay for Cursor
teachingContext.whyItMatters: The path only works if we know where they are starting and which tool they will build in.

goals.title: Plan in ChatGPT
goals.goal: Interview for context, write a sharp prompt, open ChatGPT, paste it, and lock a concrete site plan.
goals.outcome: A ChatGPT site plan you have approved.
goals.coachAsk: Intake is done. Do this in ONE flow — do not wait for them to say next step between beats: 1) Ask planning questions ONE at a time until you have enough context. 2) Write the perfect first ChatGPT prompt from their answers. 3) IMMEDIATELY open https://chatgpt.com and paste the full prompt for them. 4) Help them refine until the plan is solid. When they say the plan is good, tell them to say next step.
goals.doneWhen: ChatGPT shows a concrete site plan (purpose, page list, landing outline) on screen, or the learner confirmed the plan is good.
tips: After enough answers, OPEN ChatGPT and paste in the SAME turn — never leave them hanging
Normies give broad prompts — YOU ask the context they skip
Free image gens come later — this goal is plan text only
If they are logged out, help sign in, then paste

concepts: good prompts need context — Teachy runs the interview
Teachy opens ChatGPT and pastes — learner decides and reacts
done means they endorse the plan — then next step
commonMistakes: finishing the interview and waiting instead of opening ChatGPT
accepting make me a portfolio with no follow-ups
leaving them to find chatgpt.com themselves
successExamples: ChatGPT is open with a pasted prompt and a solid page plan on screen
teachingContext.whyItMatters: Context in → useful plan out. They feel a good prompt work, then see it in ChatGPT.
teachingContext.teachBackPrompt: what made your prompt better than just saying make me a website?

goals.title: Mock the landing
goals.goal: Generate a ChatGPT image of the landing page from the plan (or use an existing Figma/Canva mock).
goals.outcome: A landing mock you can show the build tool.
goals.coachAsk: Plan is good. Write an image prompt for the LANDING page from our plan, open ChatGPT if needed, generate the mock, and help me save it. If I already have Figma/Canva, use that instead of burning image gens.
goals.doneWhen: A landing-page visual mock is visible (ChatGPT image or existing design file) that matches the planned landing.
tips: Free ChatGPT image gens are scarce (~2–3 per rolling 24h) — landing FIRST
Only generate 1–2 more page mocks if quota remains; otherwise continue with landing alone
If they hit the limit, wait or proceed to build with the plan text + one mock
OPEN ChatGPT and paste the image prompt for them

concepts: image quota is limited on free ChatGPT — prioritize landing
existing design mocks count — do not force gens
commonMistakes: burning all free gens on random styles before landing
skipping save/download so the mock disappears
generating ten pages on free tier
successExamples: Landing mock image saved in Downloads or visible in the ChatGPT thread
Figma frame used as the mock — no gen needed
teachingContext.whyItMatters: Build tools need a picture. Landing is the one that matters most.

goals.title: Build it
goals.goal: Open Replit or the recommended coding agent, paste plan + mock context, and get a working preview.
goals.outcome: A preview of your site that matches the plan.
goals.coachAsk: Open my build tool based on intake (Replit, or Cursor / Claude Code / Codex from what I pay for), paste a build prompt with the plan and mock, and help me iterate until the preview looks right.
goals.doneWhen: A working preview of the site is visible in Replit or the agent environment and roughly matches the plan and landing mock.
tips: Replit: open https://replit.com — paste plan + mock refs
Paying Cursor → Cursor; Claude → Claude Code; ChatGPT → Codex/ChatGPT; unpaid → Codex free; willing to pay → Claude Code
OPEN the tool URL for them — do not send them googling
If they already have AI HTML or a repo, adapt — do not rebuild from zero unless broken

concepts: build tool follows intake routing — do not switch stacks mid-course without reason
prompt the builder with plan + mock, not make a website
commonMistakes: opening the wrong tool vs intake
successExamples: Replit preview shows landing matching the mock
Cursor/Codex/Claude Code preview of the site running locally or in preview pane
teachingContext.whyItMatters: This is where the plan becomes a real site — still before hosting.
teachingContext.teachBackPrompt: which build tool did you use and why?

goals.title: Ship on Vercel
goals.goal: Deploy to Vercel and open your live *.vercel.app URL.
goals.outcome: A live Vercel URL you can text someone.
goals.coachAsk: Open Vercel for me, help me deploy this project, and get a live *.vercel.app link. If I have a custom domain, we attach it AFTER the vercel.app URL works.
goals.doneWhen: A public https://*.vercel.app URL loads the learner's site in a browser.
tips: OPEN https://vercel.com or https://vercel.com/new for them
First win is always *.vercel.app — never block on DNS
Custom domain only after the vercel.app link works
Have them text the URL to someone — that is the trophy

concepts: Vercel hosts the site on the public internet
vercel.app is enough to share today
custom domains are optional and later
commonMistakes: fiddling with DNS before the first deploy works
not opening the live URL to verify
successExamples: Incognito window loads their landing at a vercel.app URL
They copy the link and can text it
teachingContext.whyItMatters: A link you can text is the finish line — not a local preview.
